paragraphs: I'm applying for the Cybersecurity Analyst role in Commerce. The mix of identity, endpoint, email and network security across on-premises and cloud environments is the broad foundation I want to build early in my career. I finished my B.S. in Computer Science at UC Irvine, specializing in Networked Systems, and I'm local to Irvine/Orange County. Your posting's emphasis on SSO, OAuth and MFA lines up closely with the authentication work I've already done.

Most of my hands-on security work is on CommunicAI, an AI-powered iOS app I built and still operate on the App Store, backed by Google Cloud. I implemented its authentication: Sign in with Apple with a nonce and SHA-256 hashing, Google OAuth, and email/password with server-enforced verification, plus Firebase App Check on every backend request. I wrote role-based access-control rules that block IDOR and privilege escalation, validated with 36 adversarial unit tests, and server-side Cloud Functions enforce input validation and rate limiting.

In coursework and labs I've used Wireshark and Burp Suite to study DNS spoofing, ARP poisoning, MITM and web attacks. I'm upfront that I haven't administered SIEM, Intune or Microsoft 365 security in a production environment yet; I'm studying for the CompTIA Security+ exam in January to strengthen that base. As captain of UC Irvine's NCAA Division I track and field team, I'm used to managing several priorities on a deadline.
I learn new tools quickly and document what I learn, and I'd welcome the chance to get up to speed on your security platforms and contribute. I'm available to start in Summer 2027 or sooner.
